title: Redwood Structured Output & Function Calling Demo - Helix Retail
summary: Intro + demo of Redwood structured output (JSON mode), function/tool-calling patterns, schema validation and guardrails. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (KMS/SSO/SOC2), and next steps to run a pilot and share security docs and pricing.
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot pricing and contract overview
Share SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration guide
SE to run a 48-hour benchmark on Helix sample prompts and share results
Schedule canary / pilot kickoff for week of May 11th
action_items: Avery Chen - send pricing + pilot contract - 2026-05-01
Priya Desai - run benchmark with Helix sample set and share results - 2026-05-05
Marcus Lee - share 3 canonical prompt sets and expected throughput - 2026-05-03
Sanjay Rao - confirm compliance questions and provide list of required artifacts - 2026-05-04
transcript: 00:00 - Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. We also have Priya, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
00:12 - Marcus Lee: Hey thanks, doing well. Marcus here, CTO at Helix Retail. We've been looking at structured output and function calling patterns to power some catalog automation features.
00:25 - Anita Gomez: Hi, Anita. Lead ML Eng. We're especially interested in JSON mode so outputs are predictable and can be post-processed without lots of heuristics.

00:38 - Priya Desai: Great. Today we'll walk through Redwood's JSON/structured-output features, function/tool calling, and how Console + Optimize recommend batching/quant profiles for cost/latency. We'll also touch on security like KMS and audit logs.
01:05 - Lena Torres: Quick ask — can you show a real schema example and how you guard against hallucinations or invalid fields?

01:18 - Priya Desai: Absolutely. We'll demo using a product enrichment schema: id, title, category, price_cents, attributes list. We'll show how the runtime enforces schema and how we can return structured errors when validation fails.

01:35 - Marcus Lee: Perfect. For Helix, throughput is a concern — around 500 requests per second during peak for enrichment. Also latency SLO ~200 ms p95 is ideal. Curious about hosted vs dedicated for this workload.

01:52 - Avery Chen: Good context. For 500 rps with 200ms p95, customers often start on Dedicated, especially with strict SLOs and throughput predictability. Hosted can be used for early pilots. We can map cost comparisons in the follow-up pricing sheet.

02:10 - Priya Desai: Jumping into console — (screen share) — here's the Structured Output tab. You can upload a JSON schema or pick from templates. We can attach a post-processing function or tool call that gets invoked when schema validates.

02:30 - Priya Desai: Note: our JSON mode uses schema-first validation; if the model output doesn't match, we return the response with an errors array and optional deterministic fallback. Also we support strict mode which forces model to re-roll up to N times before returning an error.
02:55 - Anita Gomez: Is that re-roll done in the same token budget? And how does that affect cost?

03:05 - Priya Desai: Good Q. Re-rolls are retried server-side and will count towards tokens; Optimize can recommend prompt reshaping, stronger temperature control, or adding function-calls to reduce retries. We show cost estimates live in Console.
03:30 - Marcus Lee: Could you show a function/tool call flow? We have an internal enrichment service and want the model to return structured payload and call our enrichment API automatically.

03:45 - Priya Desai: Sure. We'll demo a function called enrich_product(payload). The model returns a JSON matching the schema plus a function call object. Redwood can execute the call in a sandbox or forward it via a webhook to your service. You get the call logs in tracing.

04:08 - Priya Desai: Demo run now — sample prompt: "Please enrich product 1234 using available attributes and infer category". Model returns function call with payload. Console shows validation passed and function invoked. Response from enrich_product has added attributes.
04:35 - Sampler mistake: transcribed as 'enrich private' earlier in notes — real name is enrich_product, there was a slight mis-transcribe, sorry.
04:48 - Marcus Lee: Nice. On the security side, is the function invocation proxied through Redwood or does it call our endpoint directly? We need to avoid sending tokens or PII to third parties.

05:00 - Priya Desai: Two modes. For Hosted customers, Redwood will proxy calls if configured and can strip PII. For Dedicated/Private, you can host the webhook inside your VPC so calls never leave your network. We support KMS integrations so model logs are encrypted at rest and you can rotate keys.
05:22 - Sanjay Rao: For compliance, we need audit logs for every inference and function call. How long do you store traces and can we push logs to our SIEM?

05:35 - Avery Chen: We keep per-token traces configurable; by default 90 days for hosted, but Dedicated/Private can set retention. We have integrations to push logs to S3 or your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 and audit log export guide after the call.
06:00 - Anita Gomez: You mentioned guardrails — what if the model hallucinates a price or invents attributes?

06:12 - Priya Desai: We combine schema validation + grounding patterns. If an attribute is expected numeric and model returns string like "two hundred" we coerce in strict mode or reject. We also support external knowledge validators — e.g., a SKU check function that is run as part of the pipeline to verify values.
06:40 - Marcus Lee: From latency POV, how does function calling impact p95? If the model triggers an enrichment API call that is slow, will Redwood wait or return a placeholder?

06:55 - Priya Desai: You can set client-side timeouts and fallback policies. Redwood supports asynchronous function calls: the model can return immediately with a structured response and a function_call token that you process asynchronously. Alternatively, synchronous mode waits but you should ensure your enrichment service meets latency SLAs. Console shows end-to-end traces so you can spot bottlenecks.
07:25 - Marcus Lee: Can you show the API example for JSON mode?

07:30 - Priya Desai: Sure — (reading) POST /v1/generate with body: { mode: "json", schema: <json-schema>, functions: [..], model: "rw-infer-1" }. The response includes `output`, `validated: true/false`, `errors` array, and `function_call` if applicable.
07:55 - Lena Torres: Any best-practice for prompt engineering to minimize invalid outputs?

08:05 - Priya Desai: Keep schema explicit, use enumerations for categorical fields, set temperature low, provide examples via few-shot for edge cases, and use Optimize to run parameter sweeps. Our Auto-suggest will recommend quantization and batching strategy based on token length distribution.
08:30 - Marcus Lee: About Optimize — can it recommend quantization profiles? We need to ensure output quality for currency/precision-sensitive fields.

08:40 - Priya Desai: Yes. Optimize will analyze your workload (samples) and recommend model precision (e.g., int8 vs int4), kernel selection, and batching windows. For money/precision we recommend keeping higher precision or running a small LUT verification step post-inference.
09:00 - Anita Gomez: For pilot, we'd want Redwood to run a benchmark with our 3 prompt sets and 24/48 hour run at expected concurrency. Is that feasible?

09:10 - Avery Chen: Absolutely. Priya will run the benchmark. We'll simulate your concurrency and measure p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and validation failure rates. We'll include recommendations for Dedicated sizing.

09:30 - Priya Desai: Quick note on rollout/fallbacks: Redwood supports canary deployments and A/B model rollouts. If a new quantized model degrades schema validation rate by >X% we can auto-fallback to the prior model.
09:50 - Marcus Lee: Good — we want automatic rollback if quality regresses. Also want integration with our CI so model changes trigger evaluation runs.
10:03 - Priya Desai: We have eval hooks and can tie to your repo. You can upload prompts and expected outputs; Redwood runs nightly evals and alerts on regressions.
10:25 - Sanjay Rao: Re: data residency — we need EU-only data processing for some customers. Do you support region pinning?
10:33 - Avery Chen: Yes, we support region pinning at request and Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer EU region endpoints and can guarantee data stays in region under contract.
10:50 - Anita Gomez: Show me one more demo where schema fails and how the error looks in the API response.

11:00 - Priya Desai: (runs) Example: price_cents expected integer but model returns "TBD". Response: validated:false, errors: ["price_cents: invalid type string for integer"], suggestion: "rerun with coercion or call price_normalizer()". Console highlights the offending token section for quicker debugging.
11:35 - Marcus Lee: There's been mention online about KV cache and prefix caching — will that help our use case where many prompts share product description prefixes?

11:48 - Priya Desai: Yes, KV/prefix caching will help reduce per-token compute and latency for common prefixes. Optimize can detect prefix reuse and suggest cache TTL and shard sizing. For Dedicated we can pre-warm caches for your top SKUs.
12:05 - Lena Torres: Any limitations with function calling around sensitive fields? For example, we must ensure no PII is logged in plain text.

12:15 - Priya Desai: You can configure scrubbers and redaction rules. In addition, audit logs can be masked and plaintext kept only in customer-controlled storage via KMS. We'll include the guide for redaction rules in the docs we send.
12:40 - Marcus Lee: What about cost model — is function call execution billed separately?

12:48 - Avery Chen: Function calls themselves are charged for outbound request processing small flat fee plus any data egress if using hosted webhooks. The main cost driver remains tokens; our pricing sheet will show examples for your throughput profile.
13:05 - Anita Gomez: Are there rate limits for structured output mode or function-calls per second?

13:12 - Priya Desai: For hosted customers there are default rate limits but we can raise them for enterprise plans or move you to Dedicated. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput.
13:35 - Marcus Lee: Ok sounds good. Let's recap next steps.

13:40 - Avery Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood sends pilot pricing + contract, 2) SE (Priya) runs 48h benchmark with Helix prompts, 3) Helix shares canonical prompt sets and compliance artifacts, 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of May 11. We'll also share SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
14:05 - Marcus Lee: Perfect. Anything else?
14:10 - Sanjay Rao: I'll add two compliance questions in email — encryption key rotation cadence and access logs export format.
14:17 - Avery Chen: Great. Priya, any final notes?

14:20 - Priya Desai: Just that we'll capture expected validation pass rate target from Helix so we can tune models and fallback thresholds. I'll attach a sample schema and the pipeline diagram after the call.
14:35 - Lena Torres: Thanks everyone, excited to get the pilot kicked off.
14:40 - Marcus Lee: Thanks all, look forward to the docs.
14:45 - Avery Chen: Thanks Helix, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a calendar invite for May 11 kickoff. Bye everyone.
14:50 - [call ends]
